title: Evaluator Sidecar Integration and Telemetry Contract
author: Marco Chen
body:
Overview

This document defines the integration pattern, API/telemetry contract, and operational playbook for the "evaluator sidecar" — a lightweight process that runs alongside production model endpoints (hosted, dedicated, or private) to:

- capture representative probes
- run local/eager evaluations against candidate model variants
- emit standardized telemetry and quality signals
- drive local fallback and quantization-aware routing decisions

The sidecar architecture reduces time-to-detect quality regressions, improves locality of eval data, and enables private deployments to run meaningful evals without shipping raw customer data off-cluster.

Scope

This page covers:
1) architecture and responsibilities of the evaluator sidecar
2) event and telemetry schema (fields, cardinality, retention semantics)
3) SDK / HTTP contract for probe submission and evaluator responses
4) onboarding checklist for model owners and platform engineers
5) guardrails for quantized and KV-cache-sensitive models
6) regression triage fast path and runbook

Out of scope: long-term offline evaluation pipelines (handled by eval-harness batch runners) and human-in-the-loop labeling workflows (refer to the annotation charter).

Architecture and responsibilities

- Sidecar placement: deployed as a co-located container/process in the same pod/VM as the model serving process for low-latency access to model metrics and KV cache.
- Responsibilities:
  - Ingest a sample stream (shadow or sampled production traffic) and run lightweight probes.
  - Run targeted evals (syntactic checks, safety sentinels, coherence slices) within a fixed CPU/RAM budget.
  - Emit standardized telemetry events to the local agent/collector and the central eval ingestion endpoint.
  - Apply local fallback policies (e.g., disable quantized variant for failing slices) if configured.
  - Maintain a small rolling cache of probe inputs/responses (retention config; default 48 hours).

Telemetry contract (schema)

All telemetry events MUST be emitted as JSON objects matching the fields below. Event types: probe_request, probe_result, evaluator_health, fallback_action, quant_metric. Agents must attach a consistent trace_id for cross-correlation.

Telemetry table (human-readable):

| field | type | description | example | cardinality | retention |
|------|------|-------------|---------|-------------|-----------|
| event_type | string | One of probe_request/result/health/fallback/quant_metric | probe_result | low | 90d |
| timestamp_utc | string (ISO8601) | Event time in UTC | 2026-01-05T14:23:11Z | high | 90d |
| service_name | string | Redwood service identifier (e.g., text-gen-v1) | text-gen-v1 | low | 90d |
| model_variant | string | Model id + flavor (e.g., llama2-70b-q8) | llama2-70b-q8 | medium | 90d |
| slice_id | string | Canonical slice tag for the probe (see slice registry) | coherence-longcontext | medium | 180d |
| trace_id | string | Correlation id shared across events | abc123-xyz | high | 90d |
| probe_latency_ms | number | End-to-end latency for the probe | 124 | high | 90d |
| token_count | number | Token count produced | 48 | high | 90d |
| quality_score | number | Aggregated numeric quality score (0-100) | 82.4 | medium | 180d |
| fail_reasons | list[string] | Short codes for detected failures | ["hallucination_linked_entity"] | low | 180d |
| kv_cache_hit | boolean | Whether reply used KV cache | true | medium | 90d |
| quant_mode | string | "fp16" | "q8" | low | 90d |

Event semantics and retention:
- probe_request: emitted when a probe is scheduled. Minimal payload (trace_id, slice_id, model_variant, probe_prompt_hash). Retain 7d by default.
- probe_result: emitted after the probe runs. Must include quality_score, fail_reasons (if any), and token_count. Retain 180d for auditable slices.
- evaluator_health: periodic heartbeat; includes cpu_percent, mem_mb, probe_queue_length. Retain 90d.
- fallback_action: emitted when sidecar triggers a local policy (e.g., roll back to fp16). Must include justification and TTL. Retain 180d.
- quant_metric: specialized metric for quantization degradations (coherence_delta, ngram_overlap). Retain 180d.

API / SDK contract

The sidecar exposes two endpoints on localhost for the serving process to interact with:

1) POST /v1/sidecar/probe - schedule an immediate probe\Request body (JSON):
{
  "trace_id": "string",
  "slice_id": "string",
  "prompt": "string",
  "max_tokens": 256,
  "meta": {"tenant_id": "string", "request_origin": "shadow"}
}

Response: 202 Accepted (queued) or 400 with validation errors.

2) GET /v1/sidecar/probe/{trace_id} - fetch latest probe_result by trace_id\Response body (JSON):
{
  "trace_id": "string",
  "status": "completed|failed|queued",
  "quality_score": 82.4,
  "fail_reasons": ["safety_trigger_anchor"],
  "raw_response": "string",
  "meta": {"quant_mode": "q8", "kv_cache_hit": true}
}

Implementation note: the HTTP contract must be resilient to partial failures and provide idempotent probe scheduling. The SDK wrappers (py/ts) used by platform engineers should translate local fallbacks into service-level observability events.

Resource and performance budgets

- Sidecar CPU cap: default 0.25 cores per endpoint (configurable by tier).
- Memory cap: default 256MB.
- Probe time budget: 2500ms wallclock for non-blocking probes; 90% probes must complete under 2s.
- Allowed synchronous probes (blocking the main request) must be explicitly opt-in and have a 500ms budget.

Onboarding checklist (model owners)

1) Register slices: Add commonly used slices for your model to the slice registry with owners and annotation rules. (See slice-registry template link.)
2) Define quality metrics: provide at least 3 numeric metrics (coherence, safety_pass_rate, factual_precision) and thresholds for soft/alarm/fail states.
3) Provide fallback policy: default behavior on sidecar detection (no-op, fail-open, fail-closed, quant-disable).
4) Supply probe prompts: 20 canonical probes per slice and 50 synthetic edge probes for long-tail stress testing.
5) Validate resource footprint: run the sidecar profiling harness (script below) and confirm CPU/mem requirements.

Profiling CLI (example):

# Run local evaluator sidecar profile against model socket\$ ./tools/sidecar-profile.sh --endpoint localhost:8080 --samples 100 --budget-ms 2500

Quantization and KV-cache guardrails

Quantized models and KV cache interactions are frequent sources of regressions. The sidecar enforces a set of safety checks before a quantized variant is marked healthy:
- coherence_delta < 6.0 (percent point drop) over a sliding 72-hour window for core slices.
- ngram_overlap >= 0.78 against fp16 baseline for instruction-following slices.
- embedding_similarity variance < 0.03 for retrieval-augmented slices.

If checks fail, sidecar MAY emit a fallback_action to disable the quantized variant locally and mark a ticket with owner_team. Fallback actions must include: justification_code, measured_delta, recommended_action, and TTL.

Quality guardrail wiring

- Soft alarms: quality_score between warning and fail thresholds; generate eval-ticket assigned to model owner with P2 priority.
- Fail alarms: quality_score below fail threshold or safety sentinel triggered; generate immediate incident with oncall. Trigger automatic canary rollback if within a canary window.

Regression triage fast path

When a production regression is detected via sidecar telemetry, follow the fast path:
1) Acknowledge alarm and capture relevant probe_result events (trace_ids).
2) Run automated bisect: compare recent promotion artifacts (model_variant commit, quant profile, kernel version) against last known-good baseline.
3) If bisect identifies candidate cause, apply short-circuit: temporarily disable quant mode or revert to previous variant for 30 minutes.
4) Create a triage Slack thread with #eval-regressions, include diagnostics bundle (probe_results, telemetry snippets, model config diff).
5) If root cause not identified in 60 minutes, escalate to SRE/platform lead and open an incident per incident process.

Minimal diagnostic bundle (automatically assembled):
- 10 probe_result events spanning before/after regression\- model_variant manifest (commit, quant profile id)\- kernel/runtime version\- cpu/mem utilization and sidecar health events

Runbook steps (operator-friendly)

1) Identify: filter telemetry for event_type=probe_result and quality_score < fail_threshold for the affected model_variant.
2) Isolate: if kv_cache_hit correlates with failures, temporarily flush local cache and re-run probes.
3) Mitigate: if quant_metric indicates coherent degradation, trigger fallback_action to disable quant mode.
4) Restore: after fix, run 200 synthetic probes for core slices and monitor rolling quality_score for 2 hours before re-enabling quant mode.

Ownership and SLAs

- Model owner: responsible for slice definitions, probe set maintenance, and quality thresholds. SLA: respond to P1 eval incidents within 30 minutes.
- Eval platform team: owns sidecar binaries, central ingestion, and alerting pipeline. SLA: sidecar heartbeat coverage >= 99.5% across active endpoints.
- SRE: owns operational rollbacks and capacity adjustments. SLA: execute rollback within 15 minutes of approved fallback action.
